Conformers were ranked based on minimizing steric repulsion and maximizing conjugation. Key metrics included the Z-coordinate deviation of the aromatic ring atoms (lower variance implies better planarity) and the proximity of the carbonyl oxygen to ortho-hydrogens which can induce destabilizing dipole interactions or steric clash. 

Conformer 12 exhibits the smallest root-mean-square deviation in aromatic ring planarity, suggesting it retains optimal sp2 hybridization with minimal pyramidalization, ranking it first. Conformer 26 follows closely, showing a favorable amide orientation that avoids eclipsing with the phenyl ring substituents. Conversely, Conformer 5 displays significant puckering of the six-membered ring (large spread in atomic Z-coordinates), indicative of higher strain energy. Conformer 1 also shows torsional strain in the amide region compared to others. The ranking generally correlates with the tightness of the coordinate distribution for the core ring structure.
